title: Lab 3C — Route 53 advanced routing
topic: Route 53 routing policies (simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation), health checks, alias vs CNAME, DNS-layer DR vs ALB health, witcoskitech.com lab subdomains, GSA multi-Region failover awareness
format: 15 timed scenario questions (~24 min, ~96 sec each). Reinforces night-25-route53-routing.md and night-25-lab-route53-setup scripts. Answer without peeking at night-25-quiz-answers.json first.
answerDistribution: A×4 B×4 C×4 D×3 — options shuffled so correct letter varies

questions.question: witcoskitech.com uses a single A alias to CloudFront with no routing policy. A stakeholder asks for 10% of DNS answers to hit a canary CloudFront distribution before full cutover. Which Route 53 policy fits?

options.A: Weighted routing — two records with SetId values and weights 90 and 10
options.B: Failover routing — PRIMARY and SECONDARY without attaching a health check
options.C: Simple routing — add a second A record that shares the same DNS name
options.D: Geolocation routing — send roughly 10% of countries toward the canary

questions.question: GSA prod designs DR: primary ALB in us-east-1 serves api.globalskiatlas.com; secondary is an S3 static maintenance site in us-west-2. Route 53 must stop sending users to the primary when the app is down. Minimum DNS configuration?

options.A: Latency records in both Regions — Route 53 fails over when latency spikes
options.B: Failover PRIMARY alias to ALB with a health check; SECONDARY to S3 without one
options.C: Weighted 50/50 between ALB and S3 — health inferred automatically from HTTP 503
options.D: Multivalue answer returning both ALB and S3 endpoints in every DNS response

questions.question: You deploy identical API stacks in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Users worldwide should hit the lowest-latency Region. Which Route 53 policy?

options.A: Weighted routing with equal weights — latency selection happens automatically
options.B: Geolocation routing with a single Country=* default record for all clients
options.C: Latency routing — one latency record per Region pointing at each endpoint
options.D: Simple routing — Route 53 measures all Regions and always picks the fastest

questions.question: night-25-lab creates night25-failover.witcoskitech.com. PRIMARY aliases CloudFront with an HTTPS health check; SECONDARY aliases www. The health check shows Unhealthy for 5 minutes but clients still resolve PRIMARY. Likely cause?

options.A: SECONDARY record also needs the same health check ID attached to fail over
options.B: Failover requires NLB — CloudFront aliases cannot participate in health checks
options.C: Health checks only work when the hosted zone is private and VPC-associated
options.D: Clients or recursive resolvers cache the prior DNS answer until TTL expires

questions.question: EU privacy rules require EU visitors to resolve to an eu-west-1 CloudFront distribution; everyone else uses us-east-1. Which policy?

options.A: Geolocation routing — Continent or Country records for EU plus a default
options.B: Latency routing — EU is always assumed the lowest-latency choice for EU users
options.C: Weighted routing — set EU weight to 100 and US weight to zero for all clients
options.D: Failover routing — EU is PRIMARY and US remains the passive SECONDARY endpoint

questions.question: Exam scenario: apex domain example.com must point at a CloudFront distribution. Why is an A/AAAA alias preferred over a CNAME at the zone apex?

options.A: CloudFront only accepts CNAME targets and rejects alias records entirely
options.B: CNAME records are not permitted at the zone apex per DNS standards
options.C: Alias records require a longer TTL than CNAME — better caching at apex
options.D: CNAME at apex is allowed but costs more per query than an alias record

questions.question: An ALB in us-east-1 spans three AZs. One AZ loses power; targets in other AZs stay healthy. Clients use the ALB DNS name directly (no Route 53 routing policy). What happens?

options.A: All traffic fails until Route 53 failover flips clients over to a secondary
options.B: Route 53 automatically creates weighted records for each surviving AZ node
options.C: New connections reach healthy ALB nodes in remaining AZs — ALB is multi-AZ
options.D: Clients must manually switch to the NLB DNS name to restore full connectivity

questions.question: A public website behind CloudFront must fail over to a static S3 maintenance origin when the primary custom origin returns 5xx. You want edge-level origin failover without changing DNS. Which approach?

options.A: Route 53 geolocation records that switch origins whenever HTTP status is 5xx
options.B: API Gateway stage cache that serves a maintenance page after origin timeouts
options.C: Weighted Route 53 records that shift 100% of traffic after a short 60s TTL
options.D: CloudFront origin group with primary/secondary origins and failover status codes

questions.question: Route 53 health check on https://witcoskitech.com/HTML/index.html reports Healthy while the ALB behind a separate api.example.com returns 502. Why can both be true?

options.A: One health check monitors the static site; ALB target health is separate
options.B: Route 53 health checks always mirror ALB target-group health automatically
options.C: HTTPS health checks cannot run against CloudFront distributions at all
options.D: Health checks only apply to failover SECONDARY records, never PRIMARY

questions.question: You want Route 53 to return up to eight healthy A record IPs so clients pick one at random. No Application Load Balancer in the design. Which policy?

options.A: Weighted routing with eight equal weights on the same DNS name
options.B: Multivalue answer routing with health checks on each IP record
options.C: Latency routing with eight Regions registered in a single account
options.D: Geoproximity routing with bias set to zero in every AWS Region

questions.question: You need active-active multi-Region API endpoints so healthy Regions keep receiving traffic, and unhealthy ones are removed from DNS answers. Which Route 53 design fits best?

options.A: Simple routing with one A record that lists every Regional ALB IP in the answer
options.B: Failover PRIMARY/SECONDARY only — secondary stays completely idle until primary fails
options.C: Latency or weighted records with health checks so unhealthy endpoints are skipped
options.D: Private hosted zone associated to every VPC — public internet clients resolve internally

questions.question: GSA compares Route 53 latency routing vs AWS Global Accelerator for worldwide API traffic. Best differentiator for the exam?

options.A: Route 53 latency works only with CloudFront; Global Accelerator only with ALB
options.B: Global Accelerator cannot health-check endpoints at all; Route 53 always can
options.C: Latency routing requires health checks; Global Accelerator never evaluates health
options.D: Global Accelerator uses static anycast IPs and edge steering; Route 53 is DNS-level

questions.question: Hybrid exam: on-prem servers must resolve internal-only hostnames like db.corp.local inside the VPC while public users resolve globalskiatlas.com on the internet. Which Route 53 feature for internal names?

options.A: Private hosted zone associated with the VPC for internal DNS names
options.B: Public hosted zone with geolocation routing for corp.local records
options.C: Latency routing on the apex domain to prefer on-premises resolvers
options.D: CloudFront alternate domain name registered for db.corp.local hosts

questions.question: Failover PRIMARY points to an ALB alias. Operators want Route 53 to fail over when any single unhealthy target remains behind the ALB. What is the exam-accurate approach?

options.A: Set ALB health-check interval to 1 second — Route 53 inherits it automatically
options.B: Use calculated/child health checks that evaluate ALB target health conditions
options.C: Use weighted routing — unhealthy targets automatically receive weight zero
options.D: Attach the health check only to the SECONDARY record, never PRIMARY

questions.question: night-25-lab uses night25-simple.witcoskitech.com with simple routing (one alias). Production apex witcoskitech.com uses the same pattern. What changes when you add weighted records on a different subdomain?

options.A: Simple routing on the apex is replaced by weighted policy at the whole zone level
options.B: CloudFront requires a new distribution for each routing policy type that you add
options.C: Nothing on apex — routing policy is per record name; subdomains stay independent
options.D: Health checks become mandatory for every record set defined in that hosted zone
